title: Playbook.json (draft v3.3, schema_version 1)
description: Process configuration for agent systems. DRAFT v3.3, not normative until frozen; see spec/process-configuration.md. A playbook is data only: it never names a program, script, webhook or URL (spec section 8.5). The schema refuses URLs and shell syntax in hook arguments, schedule fields, event signers and package pins, and checks the arguments of the field, delivery.checks-passed and delivery.integration-evidence guards and of the delivery.integrate action; the per-hook argument schemas of the other provider hooks come with the provider modules (PC1). Keys starting with x- are reserved for extensions and ignored by the kernel.

name.description: Playbook name. Required for a published template; optional in a project file.

extends.description: Single parent playbook (spec section 7.1). The object form pins the parent by its Curator package identity, which the resolver compares with the lock entry of the skill that carries the template (spec section 8.2).

uses.description: Composition of several playbooks into one process (spec section 7.2).

slots.description: Abstract element types this playbook refers to without defining them; a composing project binds each slot to a concrete type.

bind.description: Bindings in a composing project: key is <playbook>.<slot> (or <slot> when unambiguous); value is a concrete entity type, or for a process slot a playbook name of the composition (spec sections 6.5, 7.2).

root.description: Role alias of the orchestrator that owns this process.

tools.description: Tool names bound to commands exported by skills installed through Curator (spec section 8.5). A template's binding is admitted only when its orchestrator skill's manifest declares the provider in runtime mode narrowed to that command. A project may rebind a tool. A bound tool runs only when the project lists it in policy.enable.tools.

people.description: Human groups named by human roles (who), mapped to waggle operator principals (op:) only (spec section 4.2). Project only; read from the committed file at the pinned revision. Patterns are counted against the roster at the same revision.

services.description: Project only: signer groups named by event declarations (signed_by), mapped to the service principals of the bridges allowed to sign those events (spec section 6.9). The service principal kind comes with the waggle amendment A1, decided on 2026-09-24 and implemented with CM2 (spec section 17).

events.description: External events this playbook reacts to. Each names a signer group; only the project binds the group to principals (services), so package bytes never choose who may sign (spec section 6.9).

field-name.description: Field names use snake_case, like task-board's task_class.

qualified.description: A name, optionally qualified by its playbook when a composition makes it ambiguous.

relative-path.description: A portable relative path inside a package; no scheme, no parent segments.

argument-value.description: A hook, schedule or field argument: a number, a boolean, null, a short string without a URL scheme or shell syntax, or a list or map of those. Per-hook argument schemas come with the provider modules (PC1).

argument-key.description: Argument names; names that would select a program, an environment or an endpoint are refused.

package-identity.description: A Curator package identity (curator-spec protocol/skillfile-sources.md): a network git snapshot, a local snapshot digest, or a configured git source.

repository.description: Canonical host/path identity, without a scheme (curator-spec core section 6.1).

duration.description: ISO 8601 duration, for example PT15M or P1W.

ui.description: Layout and presentation hints for a visual constructor. Ignored by the kernel and excluded from the semantic digest.

kind.description: type: an entity type the project binds; process: a receiving process the project binds to a playbook of the composition or another board.

requires.description: Contract the bound type must satisfy: named estimate dimensions, fields, terminal states.

writes.description: Fields this playbook's orchestrator writes on the bound type. Binding the slot grants a field-scoped lease on exactly these fields; every other write into another orchestrator's scope goes through that orchestrator (spec section 7.2).

need.description: A requirement (in require) or a preference (in prefer) stated in portable terms: agent-selection S1's vocabulary plus speed. Never a concrete model id, runtime or effort (effort lives in the operator file; a project may set a floor in policy.effort_floor). Speed terms are evaluated against measured facts, else the registry's declared typical ranges, else they are unknown (spec section 9).

capabilities.description: Model capabilities from the module registry's vocabulary, for example tool-use.

context_window.description: Context window in tokens. Replaces context_window_min.

reasoning.description: true: the model row accepts a reasoning effort (agent-selection spells the hard form reasoning: required).

not_same_publisher_as.description: Independence: differ from the publisher recorded in the provenance of the run of that role that produced the evidence under review (spec section 9). In prefer it ranks rows of another publisher first.

pp.description: Prompt processing speed in tokens per second, measured at the reference prompt size (spec section 9).

tg.description: Token generation speed in tokens per second (spec section 9).

ttft.description: Time to first token in seconds, measured at the reference prompt size (spec section 9).

class.description: Requirement class (agent-selection section 3); defaults to the role's workload class.

oneOf.description: The nearest ancestor of this type.

approval.description: Defaults for an ask approval: its scope and expiry. The approval binds to the approving principal and that principal's own runs; an operator may answer it in advance in the operator file's [answers] (spec section 9).

degraded_state.description: degrade: the statically declared review state the degraded path goes through; the next exit from the state the degraded run worked in is redirected here (spec section 9).

skill.description: agent: the role skill, by installed skill name. Role skills install with Curator activation on-demand and reach only the launches that run their role (spec section 8.1).

who.description: human: a group of the project people map.

tool.description: tool: a tool name bound in the tools map to a command exported by an installed skill.

process.description: process: the receiving process, a playbook of the composition or a process slot the project binds.

of.description: list: the item type (a field type name, or an entity type for ref items).

root.description: May stand at the top of the hierarchy.

derived_status.description: Status aggregates from children by the kernel; aggregated moves are not transitions, but they obey the kernel's blockers check (spec section 5.1).

members.description: Membership by link, not containment: the hierarchy stays a tree. The links are stored on this container, inside its orchestrator's scope (spec section 7.2).

oneOf.description: Any installed agent role with one of these capabilities (today's open-ended roles).

by.description: The structured role alias recorded by assignment or spawn.

oneOf.description: Each element has exactly one owner in each state; the state admits several roles and assignment picks one. Until assignment the root orchestrator owns the element (spec section 6.1).

blind.description: Helpers answer independently before the owner reveals answers (planning poker).

owner.description: Required on every non-terminal state of the resolved workflow (the validator checks the resolved result, so an extending file may override a state partially).

requires.description: Entry conditions: guards applied to every transition into this state, and to creation when the state is initial.

locked.description: Only transitions that name this state in from leave it; from * never matches it.

remove.description: In a file that extends a parent: delete the inherited state.

record_source.description: A field into which the kernel writes the source state on every entry, so a hold state can route back to where the element came from (spec section 6.1). Only the kernel writes it: no run, session or person does. The validator checks that the field's type admits every source state of the entries.

clear_on_exit.description: Fields the kernel clears on every exit from this state, so a reason recorded for one stay is never read for the next (spec section 6.1).

event.description: A kernel, module, tool or declared external event (spec sections 6.3, 6.9).

via.description: The one command that performs this transition, for example accept_cr; a transition is keyed by (from, to, via, on), and via does not restrict other transitions into the same state (spec section 6.2).

risk.description: Marks a transition whose firing policy.signatures may require to be signed: spending (it commits money) or halt (it stops work that is under way) (spec section 4.2).

resolution.description: Resolution recorded when the redirect enters a resolution state.

limit.description: Loop limit: after max firings for one element, the transition leads to then instead.

reopen.description: Required for a transition that leaves a terminal state. A human actor may fire it; the root orchestrator only when the type's initial state is not human-owned (spec section 4.2).

remove.description: In a file that extends a parent: delete the inherited transition with the same (from, to, via, on) key (spec sections 6.2, 7.1).

resolution.description: Resolution this transition records on entry; required for automatic transitions into a resolution state.

initial.description: The state an element enters on creation; creation is subject to its requires.

migrations.description: Old state name to new state name, applied to existing elements when a template update removes or renames a state (spec section 7.1).

cron.description: A five- or six-field cron expression.

review.description: The default of the element field review for new elements; routes select on the field with the field guard (spec sections 6.3, 6.8).

board.description: Elements in non-initial, non-terminal states of the whole board.

per_role.description: Per role: elements whose current state the role owns, or whose assignment.role is the role.

per_state.description: Per state: elements in the state, named <workflow>.<state>, or a bare state name for that state in every workflow.

wip.description: Limits on the elements in progress. A manual or agent transition that would take an element over a limit is refused with wip_limit_reached, so no run starts for it; an automatic transition into a full scope is held until capacity frees. Machine capacity (parallel runs, concurrent check sets) is separate and lives in the operator's runtimes.toml (spec sections 2.3, 6.8).

billing.description: Billing classes the project admits. It only narrows: metered rows also need the operator's own admission in models.toml, and without that file automatic selection never chooses a metered runtime. Absent: subscription and local (spec section 9).

windows.description: Times of day, in UTC, when this entry admits its models; outside them it admits nothing. Today's spawn.schedule.windows migrate here; the operator's [windows] narrow further (spec section 9).

allow.description: Admitted models; absent means no allow list. When several entries match a row, the most specific decides: <runtime>/<model>, then <runtime>/*, then */<model>; the validator refuses two entries of the same specificity that match one row. An entry may carry an effort range, the committed bound today's spawn.ceilings express per runtime, and time windows.

deny.description: Models never admitted, whatever allow says.

windows.description: Times of day, in UTC, when this entry admits its models; outside them it admits nothing. Today's spawn.schedule.windows migrate here; the operator's [windows] narrow further (spec section 9).

allow.description: The role's admitted models, on top of the project's lists.

roles.description: Per role: a further restriction on top of the project's lists; a role is admitted only what both admit. Today's per-role ceilings (spawn.ceilings.<runtime>.roles.<role>) migrate here (spec sections 2.3, 9).

models.description: Project only: hard model admission, for example under a vendor's or a company's security policy. Selection admits project admission ∩ the operator's [allow] ∩ machine facts ∩ needs; without an operator file the automatic choice stays inside it. Today's spawn.ceilings, the runtime set of preferred_agentic_system and spawn.schedule.windows migrate into it (spec sections 2.3, 9).

data.description: Project only: the project's data policy (agent-selection section 4): which publishers, models and billing classes may process this project's data (spec section 9).

oneOf.description: Per orchestrator role: the entity type whose current instance is its goal.

effort_floor.description: Project only: per role, the lowest reasoning effort a run may use. For a model row the effective floor is the lowest value the row admits at or above it; a row without reasoning effort satisfies it vacuously; a row with nothing at or above it is unmet and the role's on_unmet applies (spec section 9).

schedules.description: Schedules that take effect: all, or the named ones.

relaxations.description: Accept the fallback and degrade policies the admitted playbooks propose.

tools.description: Tools whose commands the kernel may run: all bound tools, including tools that later template versions add, or the named ones. A tool that is not listed is disabled and the states it owns cannot be entered (spec section 8.5).

standing_answers.description: Whether operators' standing answers (models.toml [answers]) may answer this project's ask exceptions for their own runs; false forbids them, open-ended ones included (spec section 9).

skills.description: Skills agents may install into the project without a person: audited, any skill the Curator registry lists as audited, or the named skills. Absent: agents install nothing and a person installs or confirms the proposal. Skills from unknown sources are never covered (spec section 8.6).

enable.description: Project only: side effects a package may propose but only the project turns on: schedules, automatic spawns, tool invocations, relaxations, standing answers and skill installation by agents (spec sections 8.5, 8.6, 9). Authority-bearing: a change takes effect once a person confirms it (spec section 2.4).

min_assurance.description: The minimum key assurance of each required signature. Default hardware-bound whenever the project sets a signature policy, because an agent running as the operator's OS user can obtain software signatures from ssh-agent freely (spec section 4.2).

oneOf.description: One value for every category in require_for.
A value per category; categories not named keep their default.

user_verified.description: Whether a required signature must show that a person acted: a FIDO2 signature with user verification (waggle section 4.4), or a signature from an enrolled operator companion app key (waggle A1 section 19.5). Defaults, whenever the project sets a signature policy: required for approvals, relaxations, halts and delegations; if-supported for spending, overrides and human-transitions. A project sets one value for every category or a value per category; with the default min_assurance, if-supported admits Secure Enclave and other hardware-bound keys, never software keys (spec section 4.2).

signatures.description: Project only: which human acts need a waggle approver signature, at what key assurance, and whether the signature must show user verification (spec section 4.2). Signed board acts need the waggle amendment A1, implemented with CM2; until then the validator warns about each category in require_for that has no signable form (spec section 10). Granting or revoking a delegation (category delegations) is signed whenever the project sets a signature policy, listed or not.

acts.description: approvals of a named human role; transitions out of named human-owned states; relaxations, the approval of ask exceptions; installs, the installation of audited skills from the Curator registry into the project (spec sections 4.2, 8.6). No delegation covers a confirmation of authority-bearing sections, of the operator's files or of a skill from an unknown source.

role.description: For approvals: the human role whose approvals the rule covers.

states.description: For transitions: human-owned states, named <workflow>.<state>. For approvals: optionally, the states whose approvals the rule covers; absent, every state where the role's approvals are counted.

to.description: Agent roles with capability orchestrator that may act as delegates, through the grantor's own sessions of the role unless a grant names other sessions (spec section 4.2).

ceiling.description: Hard ceilings: field conditions every delegated act must meet; a granted delegation may only be stricter.

self_approval.description: Lets a delegate approve an element that the delegate session, or a run it spawned, wrote a declared field of. Without it such a delegated approval does not count: no self-approval, as there is no self-review (spec section 4.2).

acts.description: approvals of a named human role; transitions out of named human-owned states; relaxations, the approval of ask exceptions; installs, the installation of audited skills from the Curator registry into the project (spec sections 4.2, 8.6). No delegation covers a confirmation of authority-bearing sections, of the operator's files or of a skill from an unknown source.

role.description: For approvals: the human role whose approvals the rule covers.

states.description: For transitions: human-owned states, named <workflow>.<state>. For approvals: optionally, the states whose approvals the rule covers.

to.description: Agent roles with capability orchestrator that may act as delegates.

items.description: Acts no delegation may cover: for the roles in to, or for any role when to is absent. never wins over allow.

delegation.description: Project only and authority-bearing: which human acts a person may delegate to which orchestrator roles, under which hard ceilings. A person grants a delegation record within it, for acts their own principal could perform; delegated acts count as the grantor's only when they come from the grantor's own sessions or sessions the grant names, and only within the delegation and these ceilings; acts under delegation count as at most one principal toward a quorum; everything else waits for the person. Without this key nothing may be delegated (spec section 4.2).

version_control.description: Commit acknowledgement policy. Owned by Playbook.json since v3; task-board.config.json's version_control keys are read for one release with a warning (spec sections 2.1, 14).

loop_detection.description: Threshold = max(floor, factor x median rework).

skill.description: The providing skill, installed through Curator as a runtime dependency of the orchestrator skill.

command.description: A command the provider's manifest exports. Command names are global shims, so published packages prefix them (cafe-send-order); never a free-form program string.

timeout.description: Invocation deadline; expiry fires tool.failed (default PT10M, spec section 6.11).

principals.description: waggle operator principals or patterns, for example op:alice@acme or op:*@acme.
Service principals of event bridges, for example svc:payment-bridge@acme. The kind comes with the waggle amendment A1, implemented with CM2.

signed_by.description: The signer group whose principals may sign this event; the project binds it in services.

guard-hook.description: A guard reference: a name, or an object whose guard key names it and whose other keys are its arguments (spec section 6.3).

oneOf.description: A guard by name. delivery.checks-passed and delivery.integration-evidence need their set argument, so they appear only in the object form.

own_element.description: Only when a run acts on the element it was spawned for.

role_ends_in.description: Only for runs whose role's end state is this state (today's end_status of the role definition).

applies_to.description: Limit the guard to one actor class or run shape (spec sections 4.2, 6.2).

then.description: field: compare one declared field with exactly one comparator (spec section 6.3).
delivery.checks-passed: the named check set must have evidence for the revision of the element's Change Request; it passes for an element without one (spec sections 6.3, 6.12).
delivery.integration-evidence: the integration evidence of the named check set, where a command route integrates (spec sections 6.3, 6.12).

action-hook.description: An action reference: a name, or an object whose action key names it and whose other keys are its arguments (spec section 6.3).

oneOf.description: An action by name. delivery.integrate needs its checks argument, so it appears only in the object form.

checks.description: The check set that gates the integration (spec section 6.12). Required: a set the project does not define refuses the integration with checks_not_configured, and a failed or unavailable set emits delivery.integration-failed with its rollback authorization.

range.description: A numeric range with at least one bound (spec section 9). The validator checks min <= max (spec section 10).

effort-range.description: One effort, or a range low..high on the common order minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh < max. The validator refuses an inverted range (spec section 9).

field-condition.description: A field condition: the kernel guard field in its object form, without applies_to (spec sections 4.2, 6.3).

workflow-state.description: A state named <workflow>.<state>, qualified by its playbook when a composition makes it ambiguous (<playbook>.<workflow>.<state>).

utc-window.description: A time-of-day window in UTC, HH:MM-HH:MM, the end excluded; an end earlier than the start crosses midnight (spec section 9).
